title: Pioneerlytics — Console usage paths and cost decomposition demo
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Pioneerlytics through Console per-route dashboards, usage-path visualization, and cost decomposition features. Customer cares about per-API route attribution, multi-team chargeback, and alerts for cost regressions. Discussed hosted vs dedicated routing, prefix caching impact, and SSO/KMS controls. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with sample traffic and share security pack and pricing.
topics: cost decomposition by route and model
next_steps: Redwood to send security whitepaper and SOC2 attestation link (Ava)
Redwood SE to propose pilot config and sample benchmarking script (Samir)
Customer to share 7-day sample traffic and contact for infra (Noah)
action_items: Ava Martinez: Send security docs and pricing sheet — due 2026-08-21
Samir Patel: Draft pilot config + bench script and upload to shared drive — due 2026-08-25
Noah Rivera: Provide sample traffic export (7 days) and list of critical routes — due 2026-08-24
Priya Shah: Share internal success criteria for cost savings and SLA targets — due 2026-08-26
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (Pioneerlytics Head of ML), Noah Rivera (Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Finance)

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes on the calendar. I'm Ava, I'm the AE here at Redwood. With me is Samir, our solutions engineer. How's that sound? Quick round robin?
[00:08] Evelyn Park: Hi I'm Evelyn, head of ML at Pioneerlytics, we own the models and inference pipelines.
[00:12] Noah Rivera: Noah, platform eng. I look after our infra and cost ops.
[00:16] Priya Shah: Priya, finance, focusing on cost allocation / chargeback.
[00:20] Samir Patel: Great, thanks. Quick agenda from our side: console tour focused on per-route usage, path visualization, and cost decomposition, then Q&A and pilot next steps. Any changes?
[00:30] Evelyn Park: Sounds good. We're mainly interested in attributing cost to product features, and detecting regressions when a new model push spikes cost.
[00:36] Priya Shah: Also need to map cost to teams for internal billing and forecasting, ideally daily granularity.
[00:42] Ava Martinez: Perfect, we'll jump into the console. Samir will share screen.

[01:05] Samir Patel: Alright, sharing. So this is the Redwood Console. Top-level is a usage lens for the last 30 days, we can change window. On the left we have Routes, Models, and Alerts. I'm going to filter to 'Routes' — here's a list of API routes with request count, p50/p95 latency, and token cost.
[01:30] (mumble) Noah: Can you expand route names? We have a few that are obfuscated in our proxy.
[01:36] Samir Patel: Yeah, you can override the route tag at ingestion, or use header mapping — we'll show that on the integration doc. The key is each route ties to traffic paths and we show cumulative cost by route, model variant, and region.
[02:05] Ava Martinez: Note that cost attribution is per-token with breakdown for prompt vs completion plus model runtime overhead.
[02:18] Evelyn Park: Does that handle cached prefixes? We do a lot of few-shot caching.
[02:24] Samir Patel: Good question — we surface cache hits as a separate column. When KV or prefix cache hits happen, tokenized cost is lower, and the console shows both raw token generation and effective billed tokens after caching. Sometimes transcription shows 'KV' as 'k v' but it's the same.

[03:05] Samir Patel: Now click a route — this opens the per-route dashboard. On top is request volume over time, below is model split. See this spike on Aug 12? You can click the spike and it shows the path waterfall.
[03:33] Evelyn Park: The path waterfall, is that the usage path visualization you mentioned?
[03:36] Samir Patel: Exactly. It reconstructs a typical request journey — middleware routing, model selection, any reranking steps, and token counts per step. It helps you see if a new reranker added extra tokens.
[04:02] Noah Rivera: Is that data sampled or full fidelity?
[04:06] Samir Patel: It's full fidelity for the last 7 days by default and sampled beyond that. You can increase retention with the observability add-on.

[04:40] Priya Shah: For finance we need daily cost slices by team and by route. Can you produce a payroll-like CSV export?
[04:47] Samir Patel: Yes, exports are available; you can configure a chart to export route-by-team CSV with allocation tags. We also support tagging at call-time via headers so your billing can attribute to product and team.
[05:12] Ava Martinez: Also there's a cost decomposition view — it splits cost into model compute, I/O, and infra overhead (like zero GPU idle charge for shared pools), and shows unit economics per 1k requests.
[05:28] Evelyn Park: Unit economics per route would be really helpful; we need to justify model upgrades.

[06:00] Samir Patel: Now I'll open the anomaly detection panel. You can set baselines (median or last-30d) and alerts for percent change in tokens or cost. You can route alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or Webhooks.
[06:24] Noah Rivera: Can we set alerts on model variant regression? E.g. new quantized variant causing latency increase
[06:30] Samir Patel: Yes, you can set rule scoped to model version and route. We also compute impact estimate — if p95 latency jumps by 200ms, here's projected cost and revenue impact.

[07:10] Evelyn Park: On the security side, we need SSO integration and KMS for keying. Any caveats there?
[07:18] Ava Martinez: Redwood supports SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles for Console and API keys, and integrates with KMS/HSM for private deployments. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[07:34] Priya Shah: Do you support customer-managed keys in Hosted mode or only Private?
[07:40] Samir Patel: Customer-managed keys are available in Private deployments and in Dedicated with the enterprise KMS option. Hosted has provider-managed keys by default but supports bring-your-own for certain enterprise contracts.

[08:05] Evelyn Park: What about data retention and audit logs? We need 90 day logs for compliance.
[08:12] Samir Patel: We retain operational telemetry for 90 days by default; audit logs can be configured to your retention needs as an add-on. We'll include log retention options in the doc set.

[09:00] Noah Rivera: Walk me through the routing options — we have variable traffic and question about hosted vs dedicated.
[09:07] Ava Martinez: Traffic routing can be policy-driven: route by latency SLO, cost target, or region. For heavy steady-state traffic Dedicated pools are better for predictability; hosted is easier for quick launches. You can also do mixed: burst to hosted, baseline on dedicated.
[09:35] Noah Rivera: How transparent is the fallback when capacity is constrained? We need deterministic behavior for our SLA.
[09:41] Samir Patel: We have automatic fallback rules — we can fallback to a cheaper quantized variant or a model with wider latency variance. Rollouts let you define canary percent and auto-fallback thresholds.

[11:00] Evelyn Park: If we wanted to run a pilot, what would you need from us?
[11:05] Samir Patel: Typically 7 days of representative traffic (logs or a sanitized export), list of critical routes, expected throughput, and success criteria (latency/cost targets). We'll provide a bench script to replay traffic and a sample pilot config.
[11:22] Priya Shah: On pricing, we need an estimate for expected monthly consumption — can you show an example?
[11:28] Ava Martinez: Absolutely. Example: route X at 1M requests with average 50 tokens/request on model G-2 yields estimated tokens and cost; we can run scenarios for quantized vs full precision.
[12:00] Noah Rivera: Would you be able to run a short benchmarks against our dev model? We can provide a container image.
[12:07] Samir Patel: We can. For private testing we can accept a container or model artifact; for hosted we'd ask for an eval proxy. For Dedicated, we can run bench on reserved pool.

[13:15] Evelyn Park: Quick question: how do you surface cold-starts for models that use KV cache warmup?
[13:22] Samir Patel: We show warm-up latency and cache hit rate per route and per model. There's a warmup suggestion that recommends warm caches for heavy routes at deployment time.

[14:10] (short pause) Priya Shah: Any competitors we should be aware of? We already talked to Anthropic Managed endpoints, their dashboard is simpler but doesn't do route-level decomposition.
[14:21] Ava Martinez: Right and some teams build in-house pipelines, but the time to production and observability gap is often the problem. We also see mentions of OpenEndpointCo for self-hosters.

[14:45] Samir Patel: Back to the UI — this is the cost decomposition chart. Each bar is color-coded: model runtime, token compute, caching savings, and infra overhead. You can click to drill to per-hour granularity.
[15:10] Noah Rivera: Can we tag routes to internal project IDs and have those reflected in the billing export?
[15:15] Samir Patel: Yep—header tags map to project IDs on ingestion and are available as a dimension in exports and dashboards.

[16:00] Evelyn Park: Regarding compliance we need SOC2 and an ISO attestation; Priya needs that for procurement.
[16:06] Priya Shah: Yes please, send both.
[16:10] Ava Martinez: We'll attach SOC2 and ISO links in the follow-up. Also the data flow diagram and standard contractual clauses.

[17:00] Samir Patel: Now a quick demo of Optimize recommendations: we run profiling on your traffic shape and recommend batching and quantization candidates per route. Here's a suggested profile: route A -> use int8 q4 on 2k tokens median; route B -> keep fp16 for response quality.
[17:29] Evelyn Park: How do you measure quality impact of quantization?
[17:32] Samir Patel: We run side-by-side evals on provided prompts and compute delta F1 and response similarity. We also let you set a quality threshold; anything beyond that won't be recommended automatically.

[18:15] Noah Rivera: If we accept those recommendations, what's the rollout path?
[18:19] Ava Martinez: You can create a rollout in the Console — canary percent, time window, auto-rollback conditions. Rollouts integrate with alerts so a quality or latency regression triggers rollback.

[20:00] Evelyn Park: This looks promising. I want to make sure our product owners can self-serve cost reports, not rely on platform team.
[20:08] Samir Patel: We support role-based views and saved reports; owners can subscribe to a daily CSV or dashboard link with limited RBAC.

[22:00] (some cross talk) Priya Shah: If we need private deployment for keys and data residency, what's the lead time?
[22:07] Ava Martinez: Typically 8-10 weeks for Private with on-prem packaging, less for VPC. Dedicated is faster — 2-4 weeks depending on region capacity.

[24:12] Noah Rivera: One last technical: how do you compute per-route token attribution when a single request fans out to multiple models (reranker -> generator -> summarizer)?
[24:22] Samir Patel: Attribution is step-wise. We record token counts per step and apply weighting rules. The console shows both step-level and aggregated route-level costs. You can customize attribution rules if you have complex billing needs.

[28:00] Ava Martinez: Alright, for next steps we'll package the security docs, the pricing sheet, and the pilot plan. Samir will drop a bench script. We'll aim to kick off pilot in early September, pending sample traffic.
[28:26] Evelyn Park: Good, sounds actionable.

[28:40] Meeting wrap and quick recap by Ava.
[29:00] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard phrases, some speaker overlap, timestamps approximate. There are references to shared artifacts: security pack (link will be sent), pilot bench script (uploaded to shared drive), pricing sheet (shared via email).
